Subject: Go decision: network closure and quick smoke run

Neha —

We are scheduled to close the last mile for the VPC link tonight at 11:30pm PT. Before we give the go/no-go to our execs I need a concise list of what Redwood needs us to do during the closure window, plus what you will run on your side for a minimal smoke pass. Specifically:

- KV cache priming: how long, traffic pattern, and whether we should mirror traffic or replay a seed set
- Expected transient latency (p90/p99) during priming and first 15 minutes
- Exact rollback trigger criteria (who to call, what to flip)
- Any ACL/BGP checks we must hold off until after handoff

Attached is the list we promised (final-reqs-acme.pdf). If you can reply with a short checklist and owners we will confirm with our SRE lead. We also want a bridge number to have engineers aligned.

Thanks,

Neha / Sam —

Below is a short, actionable plan we can send to Acme. I kept each item one line with an owner and an acceptance criterion.

1) KV cache priming (owner: Marissa) — run scripted priming 15 minutes before cut (kv-warmup-script.sh). Acceptance: 80% of keys have a warm hit within 5s of first real request; no >10s tail on warmup traffic.

2) Mirror traffic for priming (owner: Connor) — start traffic mirror at t-18m for 5m, then controlled replay of seed set for 10m. Acceptance: no errors >0.5% and p95 latency within baseline+40ms.

3) Observability smoke (owner: Mina) — run smoke-cases.md (simple generate/chat/embedding flows). Acceptance: end-to-end success >= 98% for the suite; key metrics published to the shared dashboard.

4) ACL & BGP hold points (owner: Karthik) — do not relax ACLs until Redwood confirms HA route learning in both colo and customer vpc. Acceptance: BGP adjacency established and routes prefixed in route table; validate with traceroute from two regions.

5) Rollback criteria & contacts (owner: Connor) — immediate rollback if any of: sustained error rate >2% for 3 consecutive minutes, p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5 minutes, or KV priming failure. Rollback steps: flip routing to pre-cutover pool + alert both teams. Bridge contact: #redwood-cutover (Slack) and on-call SRE pager.

6) Bridge & artifacts (owner: Neha) — 30 minute bridge starting t-10m; shared drive with runbooks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-cutover.

Attachments: kv-warmup-script.sh, smoke-cases.md

I can send this to Sam with owners and contact info unless you want to tweak.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

All — quick add on the ACL/BGP item. Two practical notes to include in the response to Acme: 

- Please confirm that route propagation on the customer side will be suppressed for the maintenance window only if they intend to revert quickly; we need their explicit approval to do a transient withdraw. If they do not want suppression, we will need an extended warmup to avoid blackholing traffic.

- We will run BFD/BGP adjacency checks at t-12m and t+2m; if adjacencies flap more than twice we treat it as a critical and hold the handoff. Document the exact traceroute commands for them to run and the expected AS-path.

Also: include a short troubleshooting checklist for when p99 spikes (which is where we usually see downstream congestion). Example bullets: check ingress ACL counters, inspect prefix-sets for accidental more-specific routes, confirm NAT pool capacity.

Karthik
Network Lead — Redwood Inference
